Registered parameter relationships

Source: R/parameter-relationships.R
parameter_relationships.Rd

Inspect how named allocations, their components, fitted sources and public quantities are connected. The graph is compiled from the model declaration. Reading it does not materialize posterior draws or evaluate a prior density. register_parameter_relationships() lets a model builder declare inputs of quantities generated by its own model syntax.

parameter_relationships(object)

register_parameter_relationships(object, relationships, provider)

Arguments

object

A BayesTools_fit, a parameter map or a parameter catalog.

relationships

A data frame with character columns source_id, consumer_id and relation, and optional source_type, consumer_type and component. Each endpoint type defaults to "quantity", with its public catalog ID. A "coordinate" or "row_source" endpoint uses the exact fitted name and type of an external scale or row-callback input already declared by the native relationships.

provider

Name of the package or model builder supplying the rows. The name BayesTools is reserved. Register the returned object with the consumer. Repeating a declaration from the same provider is idempotent.

Value

parameter_relationships() returns a plain data frame with one row per relationship. register_parameter_relationships() returns a copy of the supplied fit, map or catalog with the provider's rows.

Details

Each directed edge runs from a source to a consumer. Join endpoints by both their type and opaque ID. A fit gives the default original-scale graph. Use parameter_relationships(parameter_catalog(fit, transform_scaled = FALSE)) for links to individual fitted SDs when original-scale SDs combine several covariance coordinates. Type quantity refers to parameter_catalog(object)$quantities$quantity_id. Type prior denotes a named entry in the fitted prior list. Its native prior_owns edges identify the ordinary scalar or indexed model quantities it supplies. Type coordinate denotes a declared backend input, which may be data or unmonitored. Type random_block identifies the owning fitted block. Type row_source denotes a row-shaped source by its declared node name. A native row_data endpoint identifies the row-data context of a callback that declares zero posterior inputs, using the callback's node name. Its callback_data edge connects it to the reconstructed row source. Type constant denotes a fixed numerical scale. Types allocation and allocation_component are structural vertices with identities scoped to the formula and declared owner. They remain addressable when a scalar summary is unavailable.

For random effects, sd_source connects an existing scale to its allocation or directly to a block, parent_component connects the consumed component to its child allocation, and allocates connects an allocation to each declared component. A root whose prior is owned by the allocation uses owned_sd_source. source_input identifies an input declared by a row-source reconstruction callback. allocation_weight and inclusion_gate identify primitive inputs. block_sd identifies a block SD governed by the component on the selected scale. block_covariance identifies a transformed SD that also depends on covariance structure. Other reporting edges carry the catalog quantity kind, such as var_prop, sd_total or sd_common. formula_parameter, allocation and component contain binding keys. normalization records the declared variance normalization or R2 law. block gives the declared random block for a block binding, including when its row-shaped SD has no scalar quantity. provider records who declares the relationship. All columns are character.

For an R2 budget, the realized total and its residual scale are separate inputs of the allocation. Each term is a component. Follow its reporting edges to the share, event, or coefficient (including factor cells). The individual weights of a multi-column term can share a consumer. A share's definedness, atoms, scale and draw recipe belong to its selected quantity. Use parameter_draws(), parameter_gate_states() or parameter_mixed_posterior() to evaluate it. An allocation edge records provenance. In particular, a child with its own inclusion gates can realize less variance than its incoming component was assigned.

Provider declarations describe inputs of an existing model. A provider can declare the inputs of its extension quantities or model-syntax coordinates. A quantity with a fitted prior can supply another quantity. Its own inputs remain owned by that prior. An external scale used by a fitted allocation may be an unmonitored deterministic node in the model syntax. For example, if random_sd is computed from a total SD and a fraction, register both public quantity IDs as sources for consumer_type = "coordinate", consumer_id = "random_sd". Reading the resulting relationship leaves the draw schema intact. A row-shaped source with a declared reconstruction callback retains the inputs registered from that callback. Each such consumer has one declaring provider. Native catalog quantities whose semantics BayesTools already assigns keep their compiler-owned inputs. Provide one row per input, using descriptive relation names (for example, sd_source, variance_fraction and complement_variance_fraction). Evaluation, analytic prior availability and inclusion events follow the model's actual fitted recipes. An edge alone supplies no probability law. Unknown quantity IDs, conflicting single SD sources, duplicates from different providers, and cycles in registered inputs or SD allocation chains raise BayesTools_parameter_relationship_error. Reporting a quantity under a budget is a membership relation. Such a report can describe the same quantity that supplied another input to the budget.

See also

parameter_map(), parameter_catalog_extend(), parameter_source(), random_variance_allocation(), allocation_ref(), prior_R2()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# The fitted model defines random_sd from tau_total and a budget fraction.
catalog <- parameter_catalog(fit)
tau <- parameter_catalog_resolve(catalog, "tau_total")$quantity_id
r <- parameter_catalog_resolve(catalog, "Signal{total}", namespace = "fixed")$quantity_id
# random_sd is a declared external SD source. Its draws were not monitored.
inputs <- data.frame(source_id = c(tau, r), consumer_type = "coordinate",
  consumer_id = "random_sd", relation = c("sd_source", "complement_variance_fraction"))
fit <- register_parameter_relationships(fit, inputs, provider = "MyModel")
subset(parameter_relationships(fit), consumer_id == "random_sd")
} # }
